title: RFID Student Access
tagline: Split-perimeter door access for classrooms and workshops.
summary: A badge access architecture separating the exterior hallway reader from the interior lock relay controller, backed by Zero Trust HMAC-SHA256 verification.
whatItSolves: Cheap all-in-one readers mount the strike relay directly behind the exterior cover where wires can be shorted. Splitting reader and lock controller keeps the actuator inside the locked room.
highlights: Exterior reader never carries electric strike relay wiring
Interior ESP32 node communicates over TLS + HMAC-SHA256 with Eggman.IoT.Bridge
Firmware builds verified via SHA-256 on releases.eggmanstudios.me

detailPage.headline: A safer architecture for workshop access control.
paragraphs: Labs and makerspaces should never pay cloud subscriptions just to let members unlock a room—nor rely on exterior readers where popping off a plastic cover exposes the door strike wires.
Our split-node design keeps the actuator safely behind the locked door while verifying hashed badge tokens over authenticated TLS requests.

nodes.title: 1. Exterior Reader Node
nodes.description: Mounted beside the door handle. Captures card scan events and forwards them without any strike relay connection.

nodes.title: 2. Interior Lock Controller
nodes.description: Verifies HMAC-authenticated response from Eggman.IoT.Bridge before energizing the opto-isolated 12V door strike.

bottomBar.title: 3. Eggman.IoT.Bridge (Private Tailscale Zone)
bottomBar.description: Validates hashed badge tokens and publishes audit events to RabbitMQ over TLS 1.3.

stepsSection.title: What happens on every badge scan

steps.title: Exterior reader scans badge
steps.description: The hallway reader hashes the scanned identifier and forwards the request inside.

steps.title: Bridge verifies HMAC & policy
steps.description: The interior ESP32 node signs a request with HMAC-SHA256, timestamp, and nonce to Eggman.IoT.Bridge.

steps.title: Timed strike release + audit
steps.description: Approved tokens trigger a 3-second relay unlock and emit an immutable audit log event.
